exposure: gestational age at birth (late preterm, early term, full term)
cohort: The study included 514 infants who experienced clinical signs of respiratory distress within 24 hours of birth.
finding: Early-term neonates experience similar rates of respiratory problems, morbidities, and significant respiratory distress syndrome as late preterm neonates, and they appear to have a tendency towards hypoxic deliveries with low Apgar scores.
